attributes.body_ja:
「ということだ」は、「ということ」で前（まえ）の文（ぶん）を名詞化（めいしか）して、助動詞（じょどうし）「だ」（または「です」）で、その内容（ないよう）を断定（だんてい）する表現（ひょうげん）です。「(A) ということだ」は、「私（わたし）は (A) だと聞（き）いている」という意味（いみ）になります。これは、誰（だれ）かから聞（き）いた情報（じょうほう）をほかの人（ひと）に伝（つた）えるときに使（つか）われます。この表現（ひょうげん）には、断定（だんてい）の「だ」が含（ふく）まれていますが、これは話（はな）し手（て）がどこかで聞（き）いたその情報（じょうほう）は、確（たし）かだろうと思（おも）っていることを示（しめ）しています。

「ということだ」は、話（はな）し手（て）が伝（つた）えたい内容（ないよう）を含（ふく）む文（ぶん）の終（お）わりに使（つか）われます。

「ということだ」は、主（おも）に「によると」や「によれば」など、情報（じょうほう）がどこから来（き）たかを示（しめ）す表現（ひょうげん）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。

「ということだ」が、伝聞（でんぶん）（それが本当（ほんとう）かどうかを証明（しょうめい）しにくい話（はなし））を表（あらわ）すときは、「とのことだ」という形（かたち）が使（つか）われる場合（ばあい）もあります。この二つの違（ちが）いを見（み）てみましょう。

「ということだ」- どのような内容（ないよう）かに重点（じゅうてん）が置（お）かれている。

「とのことだ」- 誰（だれ）が言（い）ったのかに重点（じゅうてん）が置（お）かれている。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

伝聞（でんぶん）の「ということだ」は、「そうだ」よりもかたい言（い）い方（かた）だと考（かんが）えられています。これは主（おも）に、「ということだ」は事実（じじつ）と考（かんが）えられる内容（ないよう）に使（つか）われますが、「そうだ」はその情報（じょうほう）が本当（ほんとう）かどうかはわからない中（なか）で、想像（そうぞう）で言（い）っているニュアンスを含（ふく）んでいるためです。
attributes.body:
Like ということ, an expression used for nominalizing a phrase in the fashion of 'the ~ that ~', ということだ makes use of the auxiliary verb だ (or です), and stresses that the nominalized phrase 'is' the case. This phrase is often translated as 'I heard that', or 'it is said that', but literally, it is closer to 'it is that it's ~'. The だ is what gives this expression a high degree of certainty, therefore implying that the speaker has heard the statement elsewhere, and is sure of its validity.

ということだ can be added to the end of any phrase that the speaker wants to highlight as being something that is known.

ということだ is regularly paired with other expressions that show the 'source' of information, such as によると, or によれば.

When ということだ is being used to express hearsay (statements that cannot easily be proven), it can be rephrased as とのことだ. The literal difference between these two phrases is as follows:

ということだ - It can be explained that (A) is ~ (more emphasis on the information).

とのことだ - The statement of (A) has been applied to ~ (more emphasis on the source that 'applied' the information).

Caution

ということだ is considered to be more formal than そうだ when reporting information that has been heard from another source. This is primarily due to ということだ expressing something that is thought to be a fact, while そうだ retains the nuance of being something that is a speculation/guess.

attributes.description: ということだ vs. というものだ vs. というわけだ

attributes.body: とされている and ということだ both report other people's opinions. ということだ has a nuance of direct hearsay: 'They say that (A)'. On the other hand, とされている presents something as generally believed or accepted. It's less about quoting someone and more about shared public perception.

second_relatable.title: ということだ

attributes.body: ということ turns phrases into nouns and often clarifies what was said, e.g. 日本に行くということ 'the fact that he's going to Japan'. Adding だ forms ということだ, which is used to report information second-hand, e.g. 来年から海外に住むということだ ('I hear he'll be living abroad from next year.').

second_relatable.title: ということだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that

attributes.body: Both convey hearsay, but differ in tone and formality. そうだ is used to directly pass on something you've heard, e.g. 明日は休みだそうだ ('I heard he has tomorrow off.') ということだ is more formal and often sounds more confident or declarative. It can also carry a nuance of explanation or conclusion, e.g. 明日は休みになるということだ ('So that means / They say we'll have tomorrow off.')

first_relatable.title: ということだ
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: ということだ and らしい ① both convey information from another source, but differ in nuance and formality. らしい ① conveys hearsay with a nuance of confidence, e.g. 雨が降るらしい ('Apparently, it's going to rain.'). In contrast, ということだ literally means 'It is said that (A).' or 'The word is that (A).', and sounds more formal and confident than らしい ①.

first_relatable.title: ということだ
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that

attributes.body: Both can report hearsay, but with different tone. とか is casual and vague, often implying uncertainty, similar to 'I heard / They say (A), or something.' ということだ is more formal and declarative, closer to 'The word is (A).' ということだ can also be used to draw conclusions (i.e. 'that means (A)'), which とか cannot.

first_relatable.title: とか
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that… something like, They said ... or something

second_relatable.title: ということだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that

attributes.body: Both use こと to summarize information, but with different nuances. ことなの means 'it's that (A)' and is often used to clarify or define something, as in '(A) means (B)' or 'that means (A).' ということだ can also be used in this way, but additionally functions to report hearsay, e.g. 'I hear / They say (A).' ことなの, without the quoting function of という, is not used to report what others have said.

first_relatable.title: ことなの
first_relatable.meaning: (A) is (Description of A), (A) means that (Description of A)

second_relatable.title: ということだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that

attributes.body: Both can be used to report hearsay (i.e. 'they say (A)'), but differ in tone and nuance. ということだ is more formal and can carry the nuance of summarizing or confidently reporting what the speaker heard. だって is much more casual and light, and can also be used at the beginning of a sentence with an emphatic 'but I mean (A)' nuance, which is something ということだ cannot do.
